AI Song Creation

Draft ·Version: v2 · Author: Jason Chen · Date: 2026-08-25 ·Guideline: Open ↗

The end-to-end flow to create an AI song on the web: compose in Simple or Custom mode, watch generation, view the result, and see the finished song appear in History.

Background
A trial run of the yco-spec screenshot-first storyboard format in this repo, alongside the existing AI-facing area specs (specs/areas/*.md). Built to test whether this QA-facing format is worth adopting more broadly.
Goal
Give QA a screenshot-led walkthrough of the Song Creation flow they can follow without cross-referencing code.
Reading this spec. This is a behavior specification for the front-end RD, not production code — the prototype source cannot be reused. Each step card shows the screenshot first, then what the user does (bold) and what the WEB UI shows, with on-screen text, rules & limits, and input/output below. On a screenshot, a solid red frame marks the click that advances the flow; a dashed amber frame marks a key point to note (hover a frame for its label). Steps carry a stable ID (e.g. P1-S2).
PlatformYouCam Muse Web (desktop) — captured at 1440px
AudienceQA
ScopeSimple compose, Custom compose, a generation-failure path, and the full set of /song/result controls (P7) — plus three independent single-screen scenarios: guest sign-in gate (P4), insufficient credits (P5), and the Trending/My Creations side-rail swap (P6).
Out of scopeHistory’s own behavior (filters, ⋯ menu, publish, delete) — see specs/areas/05-history.md
Sourcespecs/areas/03-song-creation.md, specs/areas/05-history.md, specs/00-overview.md, and the running app

P1Simple compose — happy path

Default tab. A one-line description is enough to generate.

  1. P1-S1 Arrives at /song/create.
  2. P1-S2 Taps Idea.
  3. P1-S3 Taps Enhance.
  4. P1-S4 Types or pastes text past the length limit.
  5. P1-S5 Taps Create Song.
  6. P1-S6 Waits for generation to finish.
  7. P1-S7 Generation finishes.
  8. P1-S8 Opens History from the sidebar.
P1-S1
TRIGGERArrives at /song/create.
WEB UISimple tab is selected by default; Create Song stays disabled until Describe has text.
Strings
  • Section label: “DESCRIBE IDEA OF YOUR SONG”
  • Placeholder: “e.g. A bittersweet love song about leaving a city you called home, with a melancholic yet hopeful vibe...”
  • Disabled button: “Create Song 6”
Rules
  • Create Song stays disabled while Describe is empty.
P1-S2
1
  • 1Idea
TRIGGERTaps Idea.
WEB UIDescribe fills with a preset idea and Create Song becomes enabled.
Strings
  • Enabled button: “Create Song 6”
  • Also visible once text exists: an “Enhance” pill and a Clear (×) button beside the character count.
Rules
  • Idea fills from a fixed content pool (T1), not an AI generation on tap.A pool of 12 style+scene+tempo+mood briefs, the product owner’s own copy.
  • Each tap excludes only the brief already shown, then picks uniformly from the rest.11 of 12 briefs are eligible, so the same one can reappear later — just never twice in a row.
  • The Create Song cost shown is live and scales with Instrumental.Exact amounts come from the Credit Consume MSR (References), not asserted here.
  • Enhance and Clear both hide themselves while the field is empty (P1-S1) and appear the instant it has text.
P1-S3
TRIGGERTaps Enhance.
WEB UIAI Enhance rewrites Describe in place with a fuller version of the same idea.
Strings
  • Busy label while working: “Enhancing…”
Rules
  • AI Enhance charges nothing, ever (AC-SONG-13).Confirmed — the credit pill is unchanged after use.
  • Simple’s Enhance is single-shot: no menu, it rewrites the field directly.
P1-S4
TRIGGERTypes or pastes text past the length limit.
WEB UIInput stops accepting new characters at exactly 2500; the counter reads “2500/2500”.
Strings
  • Counter at the cap: “2500/2500”
Rules
  • Typed/pasted input is capped at 2500 characters (AC-SONG-03).Confirmed via a real browser fill/paste event, not a programmatic value assignment — those bypass the cap.
P1-S5
1
  • 1Create Song
TRIGGERTaps Create Song.
WEB UIBalance is charged the generation cost immediately; navigates to /song/creating.
Rules
  • Charges on start and refunds on failure (AC-SONG-09).Exact amounts come from the Credit Consume MSR (References), not asserted here.
P1-S6
TRIGGERWaits for generation to finish.
WEB UI/song/creating shows a progress ring, step label, and an estimate while the job runs.
Strings
  • Estimate: “This usually takes about a minute.”
  • Link: “View Later” → /history.
P1-S7
TRIGGERGeneration finishes.
WEB UINavigates to /song/result — cover, title, genre · mood line, seek/transport, Like/Share/Download, Publish toggle, and a My Creations rail.
Strings
  • Genre · mood line format: “Pop · Uplifting”
  • Empty-lyrics note: “No lyrics available for this one yet”
  • Publish state label: “Off”
Rules
  • Simple mode never sets lyrics, so the result has only this fallback note, never a Lyrics panel.
  • Previous/Next stay disabled until more than one song exists in My Creations.See P7-S1 for why that never happens in this mock.
P1-S8
TRIGGEROpens History from the sidebar.
WEB UIThe new song appears at the top of the list with a Done status pill.
Strings
  • Status pill: “Done”
Rules
  • New rows are prepended to the list — most recent first.
P2Custom compose + Lyrics — happy path

Custom tab with a full lyric sheet, producing a synced Lyrics panel on the result.

  1. P2-S1 Switches to the Custom tab.
  2. P2-S2 Taps the “i” icon beside LYRICS / IDEA.
  3. P2-S3 Toggles Instrumental on while Lyrics is still empty.
  4. P2-S4 Turns Instrumental back off, then taps the Lyrics sample-fill button.
  5. P2-S5 Toggles Instrumental on again, now that Lyrics has text.
  6. P2-S6 Taps Enhance while Instrumental is still on.
  7. P2-S7 Turns Instrumental back off, then selects Genre, Mood, and Vocal chips.
  8. P2-S8 Turns Instrumental back off, then taps Enhance.
  9. P2-S9 Taps Create Song.
  10. P2-S10 Waits for generation to finish (same screen as P1-S6).
  11. P2-S11 Generation finishes.
  12. P2-S12 Opens History from the sidebar.
P2-S1
1
  • 1Custom tab
TRIGGERSwitches to the Custom tab.
WEB UIDescribe is replaced by a Lyrics textarea, plus the STYLE section (Genre/Mood/Vocal chips) and an optional Song Title; Create Song is enabled with no input needed.
Strings
  • Section label: “LYRICS / IDEA” — the box takes either a finished lyric sheet or a style/scene brief, and has a fill button for each.
  • Placeholder: “Write your lyrics here... Or leave blank — AI will generate them based on your chosen style and mood.”
  • Chip groups, all three now marked optional: “GENRE (Optional)”, “MOOD (Optional)”, “VOCAL (Optional)”.
  • GENRE offers exactly nine chips, in this order: “Pop”, “Hip-Hop”, “R&B”, “Rock”, “Jazz”, “Electronic”, “Rap”, “Classical”, “Country” (product owner, 2026-09-01).
  • MOOD offers six: “Uplifting”, “Melancholic”, “Romantic”, “Energetic”, “Calm”, “Dark”.
  • Chips selected on arrival: “Pop”, “Uplifting”. VOCAL starts with none.
  • Field label: “SONG TITLE (Optional)”
Rules
  • Custom mode’s Create Song is enabled by default (AC-SONG-01).
  • “Pop” and “Uplifting” are STARTING values, not required ones.All three STYLE fields are optional — Create Song has never read genre or mood (`isSongReady` looks only at mode and describe), and both can now be cleared by tapping the selected chip. They start non-empty so the result screen’s “genre · mood” line, which is the only thing it says about what was generated, is not blank for a user who never opens STYLE.
P2-S2
1
  • 1Supported languages
TRIGGERTaps the “i” icon beside LYRICS / IDEA.
WEB UIA popover lists the languages lyric generation supports.
Strings
  • Title: “Supported Languages”
  • Body: “English, Japanese, German, Portuguese, Italian, French, Spanish, Turkish, Chinese, Korean, and Hindi”
Rules
  • The popover only toggles on the icon’s own click — it does not auto-close on an outside click.
P2-S3
TRIGGERToggles Instrumental on while Lyrics is still empty.
WEB UIThe placeholder swaps to instrumental-specific copy; Create Song’s cost rises; the Lyrics sample-fill button hides (Idea stays).
Strings
  • Placeholder, both lines: “No lyrics needed - AI will create a pure instrumental track.” / “Describe the mood or vibe of your instrumental...” (AC-SONG-02c).
Rules
  • Two controls hide under Instrumental: the Lyrics sample-fill, and the whole VOCAL chip group.VOCAL was added to this rule 2026-09-01 (product owner: “If Instrumental toggle on, hide the VOCAL field”). It is UNMOUNTED, not disabled — an instrumental track has no vocal to pick, so the field is not applicable rather than temporarily unavailable, and unmounting also keeps it out of the tab order and the accessibility tree. Idea stays visible either way (AC-SONG-02b).
  • Turning Instrumental ON also CLEARS any Vocal already chosen, and turning it back OFF restores the group EMPTY — the earlier pick is not remembered.This is deliberately the opposite of the Lyrics box, which keeps its text through the toggle in both directions (AC-SONG-02). Lyrics can be preserved because instrumental briefs and lyric sheets live in two separate fields; there is no second vocal field, so preserving the pick would mean sending an instrumental job whose payload still says “Female”. QA: this asymmetry is intended, not a bug.
  • Enhance is absent here because the box is EMPTY, not because of the toggle.EnhanceButton renders nothing while its field is blank, in either toggle state. With text present it stays visible under Instrumental — see P2-S5 and P2-S6.
P2-S4
1
  • 1Lyrics
TRIGGERTurns Instrumental back off, then taps the Lyrics sample-fill button.
WEB UIThe Lyrics box fills with a complete preset lyric sheet, marked with [intro]/[verse]/[chorus]/[bridge]/[outro].
Strings
  • Sample-fill buttons: “Idea”, “Lyrics”
Rules
  • Lyrics fills from a fixed content pool (T1), not an AI generation on tap.10 complete lyric sheets (one Japanese), the product owner’s own copy.
  • Each tap excludes only the sheet already shown, then picks uniformly from the rest.9 of 10 sheets are eligible, so the same one can reappear later — just never twice in a row (AC-SONG-02b).
P2-S5
TRIGGERToggles Instrumental on again, now that Lyrics has text.
WEB UIThe typed text stays exactly as it was; the Lyrics sample-fill disappears, while Idea and Enhance both remain.
Rules
  • Toggling Instrumental never edits the box, in either direction (AC-SONG-02).A rule that CLEARED the box on toggle-on was in place for one day (2026-08-25) and was withdrawn on 2026-08-26 — the toggle is not a destructive control. Any older capture showing an emptied box is stale.
  • Lyrics is the only control that hides; Enhance stays and changes behaviour instead (P2-S6).The field is still sent on generation even though no lyric sheet is expected, so a result can carry lyrics despite Instrumental being on (SONG-E4).
P2-S6
TRIGGERTaps Enhance while Instrumental is still on.
WEB UINo chooser appears — Refine Idea runs immediately and rewrites the box with a refined brief.
Rules
  • Under Instrumental, Enhance is single-tap: it always means Refine Idea (AC-SONG-14).Lyrics are not supported in this mode, so there is nothing to choose between. With Instrumental OFF the same pill asks first — see P2-S8 for that branch.
  • The pill disables itself and shows a spinning icon for the duration of the call.That round-trip is the real `enhancePrompt` API call, not a local string edit.
P2-S7
TRIGGERTurns Instrumental back off, then selects Genre, Mood, and Vocal chips.
WEB UIEach group highlights the tapped chip. All three groups are single-select and optional — tapping the selected chip again clears that group back to none.
Strings
  • Chips shown selected here: “R&B”, “Energetic”, “Male”
Rules
  • At most one chip per group. Tapping a different chip MOVES the selection; tapping the selected one CLEARS it.
  • All three groups clear on a second tap — changed 2026-09-01 (product owner).Genre and Mood used to be sticky: the click handler only ever SET a value, so the first chip a user touched could be moved but never removed. Vocal was already clearable and is unchanged. QA should test the clear path on all three, not just Vocal.
P2-S8
TRIGGERTurns Instrumental back off, then taps Enhance.
WEB UIA chooser opens above the pill offering two directions; nothing is sent until one is picked.
Strings
  • Menu title: “What would you like to enhance?”
  • Choice 1: “Refine Idea” — “Sharpen the mood, tone, and detail”
  • Choice 2: “Refine Lyrics” — “Polish wording, rhythm, and flow”
Rules
  • The chooser exists only while Instrumental is OFF (AC-SONG-14).With it OFF the box may hold either a lyric sheet or a brief, so the front end cannot know which the user meant. With it ON, lyrics are unsupported and the same pill runs Refine Idea directly — P2-S6.
  • Each direction is its own API call — RD owns both refine modes.The front end only selects the `kind` (“song” vs “lyrics”); it does not define what “refine” means for either. QA should verify the returned text differs meaningfully between the two directions once RD’s implementation lands.
  • 🎨 The menu has no design yet.DP ships no enhance chooser, so this visual is WA-authored and provisional — DESIGNER-TODO A28, which also has to settle its behaviour at 375px.
P2-S9
1
  • 1Create Song
TRIGGERTaps Create Song.
WEB UIBalance is charged; navigates to /song/creating — the same progress screen as the Simple path (P1-S6).
P2-S10
TRIGGERWaits for generation to finish.
WEB UI
Same /song/creating progress screen as the Simple path (P1-S6).
P2-S11
TRIGGERGeneration finishes.
WEB UINavigates to /song/result with the full lyric sheet shown alongside the player.
Strings
  • Genre · mood line format: “Pop · Uplifting”
Rules
  • Custom mode plus typed lyrics is what produces the Lyrics panel — Simple mode never does (P1-S7).
  • Section markers ([intro], [verse], [chorus], [bridge], [outro]) render as their own lines, same as typed.
P2-S12
TRIGGEROpens History from the sidebar.
WEB UIThe new song appears at the top of the list with a Done status pill.
Strings
  • Status pill: “Done”
Rules
  • Same list behavior as the Simple path (P1-S8).
P3Generation failure

A QA hook forces a mid-generation failure so the error state can be checked without waiting on a real backend failure.

  1. P3-S1 Types a description containing the “[fail]” marker.
  2. P3-S2 Taps Create Song.
  3. P3-E3 The job fails at about 60% progress.
P3-S1
TRIGGERTypes a description containing the “[fail]” marker.
WEB UICreate Song becomes enabled, same as any non-empty Simple description.
Rules
  • Any Simple description containing “[fail]” triggers a mock failure at about 60% progress — a QA hook, not user-facing copy.
P3-S2
1
  • 1Create Song
TRIGGERTaps Create Song.
WEB UIBalance is charged; navigates to /song/creating; the job fails partway through.
P3-E3
⚠ ERRORThe job fails at about 60% progress.
WEB UIThe Generation Failed screen replaces the progress ring, with Retry and Back.
Strings
  • Heading: “Generation Failed”
  • Body: “Something went wrong while generating. Your credits were not charged — you can retry now or adjust your input and try again.”
  • Buttons: “Retry”, “Back”
Rules
  • Back returns to /song/create.
  • Retry re-runs generation from the same compose state.
  • The charged balance is refunded in full on failure (AC-SONG-09).The screenshot shows the balance back at its pre-charge value, matching the on-screen “credits were not charged” message.
P4Guest sign-in gate

A signed-out visitor tries to generate; two steps, one continuous flow.

  1. P4-S1 A signed-out visitor types a description and taps Create Song.
  2. P4-S2 Taps a sign-in provider (Apple or Google — both are mocked, no real OAuth).
P4-S1
TRIGGERA signed-out visitor types a description and taps Create Song.
WEB UIThe sign-in modal opens over the compose screen; the typed draft stays visible and untouched underneath.
Strings
  • Title: “Sign in to YouCam Muse”
  • Subtitle: “Save your creations, sync across devices, and unlock your full creative history.”
  • Buttons: “Continue with Apple”, “Continue with Google”
Rules
  • /song/create has no route guard — the page renders for guests; the gate is on Create Song itself (AC-SONG-01b).
  • Dismissing the modal (backdrop or Escape) leaves the draft intact with no navigation.
P4-S2
TRIGGERTaps a sign-in provider (Apple or Google — both are mocked, no real OAuth).
WEB UIA brief “Signed in successfully!” stage plays, then the ORIGINAL Create Song action fires automatically — generation starts immediately.
Rules
  • The guest never returns to the compose screen after signing in.Signing in resumes the exact action that opened the modal — here, Create Song.
  • The insufficient-credit check (P5-S1) runs only after sign-in resumes the action, never while still signed out (AC-SONG-01b).A guest is never shown the buy-credits upsell for an account they don’t have yet.
P5Insufficient credits

One independent screen — not a continuation of P4.

  1. P5-S1 A signed-in user with a balance below the generation cost taps Create Song (shown here: Instrumental on, raising the cost above the balance).
P5-S1
TRIGGERA signed-in user with a balance below the generation cost taps Create Song (shown here: Instrumental on, raising the cost above the balance).
WEB UIGeneration does not start; the buy-credits IAP opens instead (GL-01).
Strings
  • Title: “Upgrade Your Plan”
  • Footer: “Demo only — no real payment”
Rules
  • Insufficient credits opens the subscription plan picker for a non-subscriber, not a credit-pack purchase.Credit packs are subscriber-only.
  • The balance/cost threshold that triggers this gate is not asserted here.Exact numbers come from the Credit Consume MSR (References).
  • Recreate (P7-S5) is gated by the same balance check.Confirmed live: a balance below cost opens this IAP instead of regenerating.
P6Trending Songs vs My Creations

One independent screen — not a continuation of P4 or P5.

  1. P6-S1 A signed-in user with at least one completed song revisits /song/create.
P6-S1
TRIGGERA signed-in user with at least one completed song revisits /song/create.
WEB UIThe side rail shows “My Creations” (their own finished songs) in place of “Trending Songs”.
Strings
  • Section label: “My Creations”
Rules
  • The swap needs BOTH conditions — signed in AND at least one completed song; either alone still shows Trending Songs.
  • My Creations drops the “See all” link that Trending Songs has; each row opens that song’s own result page instead.
P7Result screen — remaining controls

Seven independent single-screen scenarios on /song/result, starting from an already-generated result — not a continuation of P1/P2, and not a connected journey with each other.

  1. P7-S1 Taps Like, then drags the progress bar to a new position.
  2. P7-S2 Taps Share.
  3. P7-S3 Taps the Lyrics icon.
  4. P7-S4 Turns the Publish toggle on.
  5. P7-S5 Taps Recreate (charges, keeps the prior song, regenerates).
  6. P7-S6 Opens a completed song from a /history row.
  7. P7-S7 Taps Use in Music Video.
P7-S1
TRIGGERTaps Like, then drags the progress bar to a new position.
WEB UIThe heart fills solid; playback jumps to the dragged position; the inline Lyrics panel’s highlighted line follows along.
Rules
  • Like is local-only — no API call, no History write (TBD-EXP-08).A user may like their own creation (resolved 2026-08-19).
  • The inline lyrics panel's highlighted line stays synced to the current playback position.Confirmed at a scrubbed, non-zero position, not just during normal playback.
  • Previous/Next stay disabled here even though this account has 2 completed songs (D-10).Every generated song shares one fixture audio file, so the player’s own “exclude the current song” filter removes every other song too — this cannot show enabled in this mock regardless of how many songs exist.
P7-S2
TRIGGERTaps Share.
WEB UIA dialog opens with a copyable public link to this song.
Strings
  • Title: “Share”
  • Body: Shareable public link to “{title}”
  • Button: “Copy”
Rules
  • Download (desktop-only) saves fixture audio as “{title}.mp3” — not the row’s own render (TBD-HIST-01, 🔒).
  • Volume (desktop-only) is a real audio slider with its own Mute/Unmute toggle.Neither opens a dialog, so neither needs its own screenshot here.
P7-S3
TRIGGERTaps the Lyrics icon.
WEB UIA separate Lyrics sheet opens as its own overlay, with its own mini player.
Strings
  • Title: “Lyrics”
Rules
  • This is a DIFFERENT surface from the always-visible inline lyrics panel (P2-S10).Both exist at once on desktop; the icon only ever appears when the song has lyrics, same gate as the inline panel (AC-SONG-06).
P7-S4
TRIGGERTurns the Publish toggle on.
WEB UIThe song publishes immediately — no confirmation step (GL-02, unlike MV’s Publish).
Strings
  • Publish state label: “On”
Rules
  • The My Creations rail below carries its OWN separate Like/Share per row.Visible in this same screenshot — easy to confuse with the main player’s Like/Share above, but a fully independent pair of controls (`toggleRailLike`).
P7-S5
TRIGGERTaps Recreate.
WEB UI
Charges the standard cost, keeps the current song in History, and regenerates a new result at /song/creating (SONG-03).
Rules
  • Recreate was completely broken before 2026-08-25 — always bounced to /song/create instead of regenerating (D-09).Root cause: `resetForRecreate()` nulled `songResult` while this screen’s own self-guard effect was still mounted, and that effect’s redirect won the race against the intended navigation. Fixed with a ref guard in SongResultView.tsx; re-verified live after the fix.
P7-S6
TRIGGEROpens a completed song from a /history row.
WEB UILands on /song/result showing that row’s song, with the row id carried in the URL as ?id= and a Back control on the stage.
Rules
  • This is the cold-start path into the result screen (AC-SONG-11).Flow state is seeded by `useOpenCreation` rather than by a generation, so the screen resolves the song from the id alone. That is also what makes Share build a link to THIS row rather than to whatever was last generated.
  • History’s own row controls (filters, row menu, publish, delete) are out of scope here.They belong to the History storyboard — this step covers only the hand-off INTO /song/result (D-02).
P7-S7
TRIGGERTaps Use in Music Video.
WEB UINavigates to /mv/room with this song pre-loaded into “Choose a Song”.
Strings
  • Section label: “CHOOSE A SONG (Required)”
  • Preloaded source label: “Song Library”
Rules
  • The song’s title, duration, and lyrics all carry over into MV compose (AC-SONG-07).This screen does not display the carried-over lyrics, but they are present internally.
{} Data Contract

Static content pools behind the Idea and Lyrics sample-fill buttons on /song/create (P1-S2, P2-S4). Not a runtime API payload — a TypeScript module RD ships as real content, not a fixture.

T1 · Preset prompt pools (`src/lib/mv/songIdeas.ts`)
JSON
{
  "SONG_IDEA_PROMPTS": [
    "Dark R&B Rock, wandering through a foggy neon alley, slow tense pulse, eerie cinematic intensity",
    "... 12 entries total"
  ],
  "LYRIC_PRESETS": [
    "[intro]\n\n[verse]\nFrost climbs the window pane\n...",
    "... 10 entries total, one in Japanese"
  ]
}
SONG_IDEA_PROMPTSstring[12]
Style + scene + tempo + mood briefs. Fills Simple’s Describe and Custom’s Lyrics via the Idea button.
LYRIC_PRESETSstring[10]
Complete lyric sheets with [intro]/[verse]/[chorus]/[bridge]/[outro] markers. Fills Custom’s Lyrics via the Lyrics button (non-instrumental only). One entry is Japanese.

The product owner’s own copy, transcribed verbatim from the two [YCM] AI Song Ideas & Lyrics sheets (2026-08-24). Do not reword, mock, or fold into `ENHANCE_SAMPLES` — that array is a different feature’s fixture. Selection is uniform-random over the pool minus only the value already shown (P1-S2, P2-S4) — not a no-repeats guarantee across a whole session.

! Error States
ErrorTriggerMessage shown to userRecoveryRefund?
Song generation failsSimple-mode description contains “[fail]” — the QA hook for a mid-generation failure“Generation Failed — “Something went wrong while generating. Your credits were not charged — you can retry now or adjust your input and try again.””Retry re-runs the job from the same compose state; Back returns to /song/create.Yes, in full (AC-SONG-09) — the balance returns to its pre-charge value.
Signed-out user taps Create SongAny compose state, no active session (P4-S1)“Sign-in modal opens over the compose screen; no credits upsell is shown”Sign in (P4-S2) resumes the original action automatically; dismissing the modal leaves the draft intact with no navigationN/A — never charged, gated before generation starts
Balance below the generation costSigned in, credits < cost at Create Song or Recreate — e.g. Instrumental raises the cost above the balance (P5-S1)“Buy-credits IAP opens (a subscription picker for a non-subscriber) instead of starting generation”Close the IAP and lower the cost (turn off Instrumental) or top up, then retryN/A — never charged, gated before generation starts
Reload mid-flowReloading /song/creating or /song/result with no in-memory flow state (SONG-E2)“Redirects immediately to /song/create — no error message, no distinct screen”Compose again from /song/create; nothing to retry, since the job that would have generated the missing state existed only in memoryN/A — a reload this deep never reaches a charge in the first place

Production trigger for a real generation failure is undefined — the “[fail]” marker is a mock-only QA hook (TBD-SONG-06, specs/areas/03-song-creation.md §8). It also only checks Simple mode’s Describe field, never Custom’s Lyrics — a Custom-mode song cannot be failed through the UI at all today.

⚠ Prototype Simplifications — NOT the production contract

Where the prototype fakes or stubs behaviour. Build the production must do column — never the prototype behaviour.

AreaPrototype doesProduction must do
Generation timingThe mock always resolves in a few seconds of wall-clock time, regardless of the on-screen “~1 minute” estimate.Real generation duration is backend-determined; the on-screen estimate must reflect the actual expected wait or be removed.
Credit balance persistenceThe balance is in-memory and resets to its demo default on every full page load, so a reload restores spent credits.A real balance is server-held: it must survive a reload, and the charge must be atomic with the generation request rather than applied client-side before it.
Prev/Next across My Creations (D-10)Every generated song shares one fixture audio file (`SAMPLE_AUDIO` in mock.ts), so the result screen’s own “exclude the current song” playlist filter (matched by audio URL) removes every OTHER song too. Confirmed live with 2 real completed songs in one session: transport stayed disabled.Real generations return distinct audio per song, so the same filter will correctly exclude only the current song and Prev/Next will enable normally once ≥1 other song exists.
✓ Design Decisions
IDQuestionDecision
D-01What source replaces prd.md/plan.md for this repo?specs/areas/03-song-creation.md and 05-history.md (the existing as-built specs) plus direct verification against the running app.
D-02Where does the Song Creation storyboard stop relative to History?One closing step per happy path showing the new row in History; History’s own filters/menu/publish/delete stay out of scope (05-history.md already covers them).
D-03Comments layer for this trial?Disabled — no Firebase backend exists in this repo yet.
D-04Show the guest sign-in gate, after the trial initially started every path already logged in?Reversed on review feedback (2026-08-24) — added as P4/P5/P6, each single-screen or a short 2-step flow rather than a full connected path like P1–P3.
D-05Where do credit-cost numbers come from in this spec?Nowhere — every RULES bullet that used to assert a number (6/12 credits) now points at the Credit Consume MSR instead (see References). Verbatim on-screen text like “Create Song 6” is unaffected, since that is a true fact about the current build regardless of what the MSR prices it at.
D-06Extra P4 steps, or separate paths, for insufficient credits and the side-rail swap?Split into P5 (insufficient credits) and P6 (side-rail swap) on review feedback (2026-08-24) — only P4’s own two steps are a connected flow; P5 and P6 are independent screens, and numbering them as further P4 steps read as if they were part of the guest flow.
D-07The negative credit balance visible in the first round of screenshots — capture artifact, or defect?A real defect, fixed 2026-08-25. The generation-start effect charged credits with no idempotency guard, so React Strict Mode’s deliberate double-invoke billed every generation twice (a 10-credit balance went to −2 for one 6-credit song, and a failed job refunded only half of what it took). Both generation screens now guard the effect with a ref. Re-verified against the running app: one generation deducts one charge, and a failure returns the balance to its pre-charge value. All screenshots were recaptured.
D-08The Enhance direction chooser had no design — ship the placeholder popover, or build the real one?Built the real one (2026-08-27). The first pass was a WA-authored anchored popover standing in for a design DP does not ship. The product owner supplied the intended UI, which matches the mobile app prototype’s “Enhance Direction Sheet” (muse-prototype-v2.html:5726): a centred dialog with a gradient icon tile per direction. Both gradients and both icon names are copied from there verbatim into src/styles/enhance-dialog.css. This answers the first of DESIGNER-TODO A28’s two questions (anchored popover vs centred dialog); the second — whether phones should get the prototype’s bottom SHEET instead — is still open.
D-09Recreate always bounced to /song/create instead of regenerating — fix now or document?Fixed (2026-08-25) — unlike Enhance, this was a complete feature broken by a state/navigation race in SongResultView.tsx, not a placeholder. Patched with a ref guard; re-verified live that Recreate now charges, keeps the prior song in History, and regenerates correctly.
D-10Prev/Next never shows enabled, even with 2 real completed songs — fix or document?Documented only (2026-08-25) — root cause is a shared mock audio fixture (every song plays the same file), not a logic bug. A real fix needs additional distinct audio assets, which is content/asset work outside this spec’s scope.
D-11How to fold ~20 newly-found QA gaps into P1/P2 without a separate "compose controls" path?Inserted as new steps directly into P1/P2 (they are sub-interactions of the same screens those paths already walk through), and added one new path, P7, touring /song/result’s remaining controls from an already-generated result. Every cross-reference (criteria, the flow diagram, cited step IDs) was updated for the resulting renumbering.
